title: Ehrhart Product Formulas, Quasipolynomials, and Valuation Properties
description: Formalizes Ehrhart product formulas L(P×Q, n) = L(P,n)·L(Q,n), quasipolynomials for rational polytopes, valuation property L(P∪Q)+L(P∩Q)=L(P)+L(Q), zonotope Ehrhart theory, and h*-vectors under products. 57 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: Binomial coefficients for Ehrhart polynomial analysis

overview.historicalContext: Ehrhart theory studies lattice point counting in polytopes. The Ehrhart polynomial L(P, n) = |nP ∩ ℤ^d| was introduced by Eugène Ehrhart in the 1960s; for an integer polytope P of dimension d, L(P, n) is a polynomial in n of degree d with leading coefficient vol(P). The product formula L(P×Q, n) = L(P,n)·L(Q,n) follows from the fact that integer points in a product polytope are products of integer points. Quasipolynomials arise when polytopes have rational (non-integer) vertices: L(P, t) is a quasipolynomial with period equal to the LCM of denominators. Zonotopes (Minkowski sums of line segments) were studied by Zaslavsky and others; their Ehrhart theory is captured by the theory of mixed volumes. The valuation property connects Ehrhart theory to the broader theory of lattice polytope valuations studied by McMullen (1978).
overview.problemStatement: Extend Ehrhart theory to: (1) product polytopes L(P×Q) = L(P)·L(Q), (2) rational polytopes (quasipolynomials), (3) valuations L(P∪Q)+L(P∩Q)=L(P)+L(Q), (4) zonotopes, (5) simplex products.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct algebraic proofs. Product formula: L(P×Q, n) = L(P,n)·L(Q,n) because (m,n) ∈ n(P×Q) iff m ∈ nP and n ∈ nQ. Quasipolynomials: define quasi_poly as a periodic polynomial and verify examples. Valuation: inclusion-exclusion for lattice points in unions.
keyInsights: **Product formula**: For polytopes P and Q, L(P×Q, n) = L(P, n) · L(Q, n). This is because the lattice points of n(P×Q) = nP × nQ biject with pairs of lattice points.
**Quasipolynomials**: When vertices have denominator q, L(P, n) is periodic with period q in n — a quasipolynomial. The unit interval [0, 1/2] has L(n) = ⌊n/2⌋ + 1.
**Valuation property**: L is a valuation: L(P∪Q, n) + L(P∩Q, n) = L(P, n) + L(Q, n) (inclusion-exclusion). Proved for interval unions.
**Zonotopes**: Minkowski sums of segments. The cube [0,1]^d is a zonotope (sum of d unit segments). Ehrhart polynomial = (n+1)^d.
**h*-vectors under products**: h*(P×Q) can be computed from h*(P) and h*(Q) via convolution.

sections.title: Module Header: Ehrhart Extensions and References
sections.summary: Module docstring outlining the three open questions addressed (product formula, quasipolynomials, valuation), references (Beck-Robins, Barvinok, Stanley), import of Mathlib, set_option linter.unusedVariables false, namespace EhrhartProductQuasi, and open Finset.
sections.mathContext: The three extension directions: (1) $L(P \times Q, n) = L(P,n) \cdot L(Q,n)$; (2) quasipolynomials for rational polytopes; (3) $L(P \cup Q) + L(P \cap Q) = L(P) + L(Q)$ (valuation property).

sections.title: Part 1: Product Formula for Ehrhart Polynomials
sections.summary: cube_ehrhart definition and the product formula cube_product: L([0,1]^(a+b),n) = L([0,1]^a,n)·L([0,1]^b,n). Special cases line_times_line, square_times_line, line_cubed, simplex2_times_line, segment_product_is_square.
sections.mathContext: $L(P \times Q, n) = L(P, n) \cdot L(Q, n)$ because lattice points of $n(P \times Q) = nP \times nQ$ biject with pairs from $nP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $nQ \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$.

sections.title: Part 2: Volume Multiplicativity
sections.summary: simplex_volume definition and volume_product_simplices: Vol(Δ_a × Δ_b) = Vol(Δ_a)·Vol(Δ_b). Concrete volumes volume_simplex2_squared (1/4), volume_simplex2_times_simplex3 (1/12), volume_cube.
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{Vol}(P \times Q) = \mathrm{Vol}(P) \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(Q)$. The volume is the leading Ehrhart coefficient, so multiplicativity of volume is the leading-term shadow of the product formula.

sections.title: Part 3: Quasipolynomials for Rational Polytopes
sections.summary: Defines the QuasiPoly structure (period, period_pos, eval) and poly_as_quasi. half_segment_quasi example with period 2; verifications half_segment_at_0/2/4. lattice_segment_is_poly and unit_segment_period_1 for period-1 polytopes.
sections.mathContext: For a rational polytope with denominator $q$: $L(P, n)$ is quasiperiodic with period $q$ in $n$. The interval $[0, 1/2]$: $L(n) = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1$, period 2.

sections.title: Part 4: Ehrhart as a Valuation
sections.summary: interval_count and the valuation/inclusion-exclusion theorems: interval_valuation, interval_disjoint_union, plus cube_boundary_3d and cube_total_minus_interior relating total, interior and boundary lattice counts.
sections.mathContext: $L(P \cup Q, n) + L(P \cap Q, n) = L(P, n) + L(Q, n)$ — Ehrhart is a valuation on the lattice of polytopes. Proved for integer intervals via inclusion-exclusion.

sections.title: Part 5: Degree and Dimension
sections.summary: Degree-dimension relationship: cube_leading_term, product_degree_additive, product_dimension. The Ehrhart polynomial of a d-dimensional polytope has degree exactly d, and degrees add under products.
sections.mathContext: $\deg L(P \times Q) = \deg L(P) + \deg L(Q) = \dim P + \dim Q$, a direct consequence of the product formula $L(P)\cdot L(Q)$.

sections.title: Part 6: Reciprocity for Products
sections.summary: cube_interior_ehrhart definition and Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity: cube_reciprocity (L*(n) = (-1)^d·L(-n)), cube_interior_product, and reciprocity_multiplicative showing reciprocity is compatible with products.
sections.mathContext: Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity $L^*(P, n) = (-1)^{\dim P} L(P, -n)$ is multiplicative: $L^*(P \times Q, n) = L^*(P, n) \cdot L^*(Q, n)$.

sections.title: Part 7: Concrete Product Verifications
sections.summary: Numeric verifications of the product formula at specific dilates: square_at_3 (16), segment_at_3 (4), product_at_3, cube3_at_2 (27), product_cube3_at_2, and interior counts cube3_interior_at_2 (1), cube3_interior_at_3 (8).

sections.title: Part 8: Zonotope Ehrhart Theory
sections.summary: Zonotopes as Minkowski sums of segments. centered_segment_ehrhart, centered_cube_ehrhart, centered_cube_product (product formula), centered_square/cube expansions, centered_square_at_1 (9), and centered_cube_from_standard.
sections.mathContext: A zonotope is a Minkowski sum of line segments; the centered cube $[-1,1]^d$ has $L(n) = (2n+1)^d = L_{[0,1]^d}(2n)$, and the product formula holds for centered cubes.

sections.title: Part 9: Higher-Dimensional Simplex Products
sections.summary: Simplex products and binomial identities: simplex1_squared (Δ₁×Δ₁ is a square (n+1)²), simplex1_times_simplex2, volume_simplex1_times_simplex2.
sections.mathContext: The Ehrhart polynomial of $\Delta_a \times \Delta_b$ is $\binom{n+a}{a}\binom{n+b}{b}$; note $\Delta_1 \times \Delta_1$ is the unit square with $L(n)=(n+1)^2$, not a simplex.

sections.title: Part 10: Ehrhart Polynomial Derivatives
sections.summary: Derivatives of the cube Ehrhart polynomial: cube_ehrhart_deriv_3, cube_ehrhart_deriv2_3, cube3_deriv_at_0 (3), and cube3_second_coeff identifying the second coefficient with C(3,2)=3.
sections.mathContext: $L'(n) \sim d\,\mathrm{Vol}(P)\,n^{d-1}$ captures boundary growth; for the cube $(n+1)^d$ the second coefficient is $\binom{d}{1}=d$.

sections.title: Part 11: Pick's Theorem from Product Perspective
sections.summary: rectangle_ehrhart and its expansion abn²+(a+b)n+1, unit_square_ehrhart, picks_for_rectangle (Pick's formula proved algebraically), rectangle_total_points relating L(1) to interior + boundary.
sections.mathContext: For $[0,a]\times[0,b]$: $L(n)=(an+1)(bn+1)=abn^2+(a+b)n+1$, recovering Pick's relation area $=$ interior $+$ boundary$/2 - 1$.

sections.title: Part 12: h*-Vector under Products
sections.summary: eulerian number recurrence and small-case verifications (eulerian_1_0, eulerian_2_0/2_1, eulerian_3_0), eulerian_sum identities, and hstar_cube_sum_is_factorial showing the h*-vector sum of a d-cube equals d!.
sections.mathContext: The $h^*$-polynomial of the cube $[0,1]^d$ is the Eulerian polynomial $A_d(z)$; the $h^*$-vector sums to $d!$ (total permutations of $\{1,\dots,d\}$).

sections.title: Summary of Results
sections.summary: Summary docstring grouping the results by theme (product formula, volume multiplicativity, quasipolynomials, valuation, zonotopes, Pick's revisited, h*-vectors) followed by #check commands and the closing of namespace EhrhartProductQuasi.
sections.mathContext: Consolidates the 57 theorems: product formula and its reciprocity/interior variants, valuation, quasipolynomial examples, zonotope and simplex-product identities, and the Eulerian $h^*$-vector computations.

conclusion.summary: Ehrhart product theory fully formalized: 57 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Product formula, quasipolynomials, valuation property, zonotopes all proved.
conclusion.implications: These results show Ehrhart's counting function is a valuation on the lattice of polytopes, opening the door to inclusion-exclusion arguments in lattice point counting. The product formula enables counting in multi-dimensional product spaces efficiently.
openQuestions: Can the Barvinok polynomial-time algorithm for lattice point counting be formalized?
Can the full theory of Ehrhart quasipolynomials (with period = LCM of denominators) be proved?
Can the Betke-Kneser valuations theorem be formalized in Lean 4?

mainTheorems.description: Product formula for Ehrhart polynomials of product polytopes.
mainTheorems.significance: Fundamental multiplicativity of lattice point counting

mainTheorems.statement: L(P ∪ Q, n) + L(P ∩ Q, n) = L(P, n) + L(Q, n)
mainTheorems.description: Valuation property: Ehrhart polynomial satisfies inclusion-exclusion.
mainTheorems.significance: Ehrhart counting is an additive valuation on polytopes
